definition: Gradual withdrawal is a progressive pulling back from society, seen as increasing difficulty staying engaged or reachable over time. In the source, it is reflected in reduced social participation and interaction, ranging from lower involvement in groups to social isolation.

reasons: The definition adds an unsupported interpretation that gradual withdrawal means “increasing difficulty staying engaged or reachable over time”; the packet only describes stages of follow-up difficulty and associated social participation/interaction patterns, not that specific behavioral meaning.
It generalizes from the study’s older-adult follow-up context to a broader clinical definition without support from the packet.

The packet does not provide a direct definition of “gradual withdrawal”; it describes a study about “gradual withdrawal from society” operationalized via “stages of follow-up difficulty,” but the definition’s phrasing (“progressive pulling back from society,” “difficulty staying engaged or reachable”) is interpretive rather than explicitly supported.

The definition mentions a spectrum (“ranging from lower involvement in groups to social isolation”), while the packet only reports associations with baseline social participation variables across stages/groups and a “social isolation” characterization for the non-respondent group; the full “spectrum” framing is not stated as such.
